MassRobotics plans Boston Harbor marine robotics facility for early 2028

The Fish Pier site will connect prototyping with water testing, with a tank and launch equipment; programming is planned during 2027.

The Robot Report ↗20 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A new waterfront development site

MassRobotics is developing a marine robotics facility at Boston Fish Pier with the Massachusetts Port Authority, or Massport. Construction is underway, with opening targeted for early 2028 and programming planned during 2027. These are future milestones; the announcement does not mean the complete facility is already operating.

Connecting fabrication with water access

Planned equipment includes a water tank, a float alongside the pier for direct water testing, and lifting and launch equipment. Teams using the nearby MassRobotics machine shop would be able to move prototypes to the harbor. The arrangement is intended to reduce the difficulty of renting boats, borrowing tanks or traveling to distant test sites.

Infrastructure for marine startups

MassRobotics says it supports more than 100 resident startups. CRABI Robotics, which develops underwater hull-cleaning robots, illustrates the kinds of companies that could benefit. Nearby water access could shorten build-and-test cycles, although the report provides no facility pricing, membership conditions or measured cost savings from the new site.
